title: Where Bunk was after the first Stuyvesant engagement
summary: They try to sort out Bunk's movements and dates after 1946, with Russell consulting his notes.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So I guess I might have approached him at that time about lessons. I don't recall. But anyway, when I finally moved up to New York, Monk was living up there and in between jobs, I guess, at the time. Did he stay in New York after the second engagement?

No, no, he went right back in June. His wife was there and they went back, oh, within two or three days after the Stuyvesant engagement closed. That's when he made those records with Don and the drummer.
Steele. And then went back about the next day or two after that, I think.
Well, anyway, he must have come back a few months later, maybe for a single concert or something.

Well, I don't think it was William. It was quite a while later, if I remember rightly. That was 1946. He went to Chicago later that year. In the fall, he went to Chicago. I don't remember that he went to New York that next fall. You don't remember your dates exactly, you say, on some of that.
No, I'm very vague about the dates.
It might have been 1947 before he got back to New York.
It could very well have been. I'm trying to remember what else was going on then, but I can't think of anything to place
it. Anyway, I have some of that in my notes pretty well dated, I think, with letters from Gene Williams and other people about his activities.
I remember one time Bunk flew up from New Orleans to play a concert for Maltz, but I think that was after that. I think that was after he went down. Unless maybe that...
That was... Yeah, that wouldn't be before 1947, hardly, I don't believe.
